answer: Sealed-bid capability auction: identities bid scarce compute slots to register, paying the clearing price even if they lose. Bids are sealed until a fixed block height, so a subsidized tundra of fake identities cannot cheaply probe the price and must commit real resources blind. At the auction's zenith, losing bids forfeit a fraction to the protocol, making each additional identity cost the expected clearing price times the forfeit rate. This caps the summit of profitable sybils, since marginal identities pay more than any per-identity revenue.
